question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

Always keep in mind leaner bodies need more calories than fattest ones.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. fatter.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word "than" is a marker of the comparative degree. When two things are compared with "than", the adjective must be in the comparative form. The comparative of "fat" is "fatter".

◦ Correct: ... leaner bodies need more calories than fatter ones.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "fat" is the positive degree and cannot be used with "than".

• Option 2 "more fatter" is a double comparative — always wrong.

• Option 3 "the fattest" is the superlative and is used with "the", not "than".

NOTE

• Degrees of comparison of "fat": fat – fatter (with "than") – fattest (with "the"). Short adjectives ending in a single vowel + consonant double the last letter: fat → fatter, big → bigger, thin → thinner.

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word.

I did not like his bossy attitude.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. controlling.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Bossy" means fond of giving orders; domineering and always telling others what to do. Its closest synonym is "controlling". (हुक्म चलाने वाला / दबंग)

◦ Example: Her bossy/controlling manner annoyed the whole team.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "idiosyncratic" (peculiar/individual), Option 2 "sensible" (practical and wise) and Option 4 "benevolent" (kind and generous) do not match "bossy".

NOTE

• Synonyms of bossy: controlling, domineering, overbearing, dictatorial, authoritarian. Antonyms: submissive, meek, easy-going.

question:
Select the correct spelling from the given options to fill in the blank.

We ________ to keep you informed of any delay to your expected delivery date.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. endeavour.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Endeavour" (British spelling) means to try hard / to make an earnest effort to do something. It is also a noun meaning a serious attempt. (प्रयास करना)

◦ Correct: We endeavour to keep you informed of any delay to your expected delivery date.

• Spelling key: EN + DEA + VOUR.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• The other options are misspelt: "endevour", "endevor" and "endavour" are all incorrect.

• American spelling is "endeavor" (without the "u"); British is "endeavour".

NOTE

• Similar British "-our" words: colour, favour, honour, labour, behaviour, neighbour. American English drops the "u": color, favor, honor.

question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined words in the given sentence.

I have never had and never will be dependent on him.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. never been.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence needs parallel structure with the future part "never will be dependent". The verb "be" must be completed for the present-perfect part too: "I have never been ... and never will be dependent on him."

◦ Correct: I have never been and never will be dependent on him.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• "have never had" is wrong because "had" cannot combine with "dependent" the way "been" can; the correct auxiliary + participle is "have + been".

• Options 1, 2 and 4 break the parallel construction required with "never will be".

NOTE

• When two clauses share a complement (here "dependent on him"), both verb forms must fit it: "have never been ... and never will be ..." (present perfect + future, both using "be").

question:
Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for highlighted group of words in the given sentence.

He devoted his entire life to the study of the human mind.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. psychology.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Psychology" is the scientific study of the human mind and behaviour. So the study of the human mind = psychology. (मनोविज्ञान)

◦ Example: A psychology student learns how the mind influences behaviour.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "physics" (study of matter and energy), Option 3 "philology" (study of the history of languages) and Option 4 "physiology" (study of the functions of living organisms/body) do not refer to the mind.

NOTE

• Useful "-logy" words: psychology (mind), physiology (body functions), philology (languages), sociology (society), zoology (animals), anthropology (human societies).

question:
Select the option that rectifies the INCORRECT spelling in the given sentence.

If you try to conwince people that money is not very important, then you are barking up the wrong tree.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. convince.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The misspelt word "conwince" should be spelt "convince", meaning to persuade someone to believe or do something. (विश्वास दिलाना / मनाना)

◦ Correct: If you try to convince people that money is not very important, then you are barking up the wrong tree.

• Spelling key: CON + VINCE.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• The other options are wrong spellings: "conveence", "canvince" and "convincee" are all incorrect.

• The idiom "barking up the wrong tree" means to pursue a mistaken or misguided line of thought/action.

NOTE

• Related words: convince (verb), conviction (noun), convincing (adjective). Do not confuse "convince" with "convey" (to communicate).

question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

If I wrote an email / to my boss now, / he will react / by yelling at me tomorrow in the morning.
option_3: by yelling at me tomorrow in the morning.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. If I wrote an email.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• This is a Second Conditional (unreal present/future) sentence. The structure is: If + past simple, ... would + base verb. The main clause here uses "will react", so the if-clause should use the past simple correctly and the result clause should use "would". The error lies in the mismatch: with "he will react" (real/first conditional), the if-clause should be "If I write an email". As written, "If I wrote ... he will react" is inconsistent.

◦ Correct (First Conditional): If I write an email to my boss now, he will react ...

◦ Correct (Second Conditional): If I wrote an email to my boss now, he would react ...

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• The tense clash makes the conditional grammatically incorrect; the segment "If I wrote an email" carries the error because it does not agree with "he will react".

NOTE

• First Conditional: If + present simple, will + V1 (real/likely). Second Conditional: If + past simple, would + V1 (imaginary/unreal). The if-clause and result clause must belong to the same type.

question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

Rahul was angry of his brother as he broke his pen.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. at.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correct prepositional collocation is "angry at/with somebody" (for a person) and "angry about something". "Angry of" is incorrect. The best substitution here is "at".

◦ Correct: Rahul was angry at his brother as he broke his pen.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• "angry from" and "angry on" are non-standard.

• We are "angry with a person" or "angry at a person/thing" and "angry about a situation".

NOTE

• Prepositions with "angry": angry at/with (a person), angry about (a thing/situation). Similar: annoyed with, furious at, irritated by.

question:
Select the most appropriate idiom that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

We often go camping, but I have never been to that particular part of town or country before.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. neck of the woods.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "neck of the woods" means a particular area or locality / a specific part of a place. It fits "that particular part of town or country". (कोई विशेष क्षेत्र / इलाका)

◦ Example: What brings you to this neck of the woods?

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "knock on wood" (said to avoid bad luck), Option 3 "get it in the neck" (to be severely scolded/punished) and Option 4 "risk one's neck" (to put oneself in danger) do not fit.

NOTE

• "Neck of the woods" is an informal expression for a neighbourhood or region, especially one that is far or unfamiliar.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank .

The company's decision to relocate had a negative ___________ on its employees.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. effect.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Effect" (a noun) means a result or influence of something. The phrase "had a negative effect on" means it influenced them negatively. (प्रभाव / असर)

◦ Correct: The company's decision to relocate had a negative effect on its employees.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "accommodation" (lodging) and Option 4 "conclusion" (an ending) do not fit "had a negative ___ on".

• Option 2 "establish" is a verb, but a noun is needed after "a negative".

NOTE

• Note the difference: effect (noun — a result) vs affect (verb — to influence). "The decision affected employees" / "The decision had an effect on employees".

question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom from the alternatives.

Rajiv will understand some day that all his friends are fair weather friends.
option_1: A friend who stays only when times are convenient
option_2: True friends help you when you need them
option_3: A friend who meets you only during pleasant weather
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. A friend who stays only when times are convenient.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "fair weather friend" means a person who is a friend only when things are going well and deserts you in difficult times. (मतलबी दोस्त / सुख का साथी)

◦ Example: When he lost his job, his fair weather friends disappeared.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 3 takes the phrase literally ("pleasant weather") and misses the figurative sense.

• Options 2 and 4 describe the opposite or an unrelated idea.

NOTE

• A "fair weather friend" is unreliable in hardship. Contrast: "A friend in need is a friend indeed" — a true friend helps in difficulty.

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word.

Collapse
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Fall.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Collapse" means to fall down or give way suddenly; to break down. Its closest synonym is "fall". (ढह जाना / गिर पड़ना)

◦ Example: The old bridge collapsed/fell during the flood.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Surprise", Option 2 "Jump" and Option 3 "Side" are unrelated to the meaning of collapse.

NOTE

• Synonyms of collapse: fall, cave in, crumble, give way, break down. It can also mean to faint (the patient collapsed) or to fail (the deal collapsed).

question: Select the sentence that has a grammatical error.
option_1: They have an information about the event.
option_2: The cat is sleeping on a mat.
option_3: She is an artist at a local gallery.
option_4: Can you bring me the keys to the car?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. They have an information about the event.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Information" is an uncountable (non-count) noun. It cannot be used with the article "an" or made plural. So "an information" is wrong; it should simply be "information" or "some information / a piece of information".

◦ Correct: They have information (or some information / a piece of information) about the event.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Options 2, 3 and 4 are grammatically correct.

NOTE

• Common uncountable nouns that take no "a/an" and no plural: information, advice, furniture, equipment, luggage, news, work, knowledge, evidence. Use "a piece of information/advice" to count them.

question:
Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the underlined word.

The old library had a musty smell from years of neglect.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. stale.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Musty" means having a stale, mouldy or damp smell, especially due to lack of fresh air. Its closest synonym is "stale". (बासी / सीलनभरी गंध वाला)

◦ Example: The closed room had a musty/stale odour.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "casual" (informal) and Option 2 "foggy" (misty) are unrelated.

• Option 4 "fresh" is the antonym of musty.

NOTE

• Synonyms of musty: stale, mouldy, dank, fusty, stuffy. Antonym: fresh, airy.

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word.

compassionate
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. cruel.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Compassionate" means feeling or showing sympathy and concern for others; kind and merciful. Its antonym is "cruel", meaning heartless and causing suffering. (दयालु का विलोम — निर्दयी)

◦ Example: A compassionate nurse vs a cruel tyrant.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Options 2 "confident", 3 "hardworking" and 4 "disciplined" are unrelated qualities, not opposites of compassionate.

NOTE

• Synonyms of compassionate: kind, merciful, sympathetic, humane, caring. Antonyms: cruel, merciless, heartless, ruthless.

question:
The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don't find any error, mark 'No error' as your answer.

If the players don't wear sunscreen, / their faces will / get reddest.
option_4: If the players don't wear sunscreen,
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. get reddest.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence is comparing a result caused by not wearing sunscreen, not comparing three or more things, so the superlative "reddest" is wrong. It should be the comparative "redder" (their faces will get redder than before).

◦ Correct: If the players don't wear sunscreen, their faces will get redder.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• "If the players don't wear sunscreen," and "their faces will" are grammatically correct (First Conditional: If + present, will + V1).

NOTE

• Use the comparative (-er / more) when comparing two situations or showing change; use the superlative (-est / most) when comparing three or more or picking the extreme of a group. "get redder" (change) vs "the reddest of all" (extreme).

question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

Effective responses of climate change are imperative to protect the world's children and fulfil their rights.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. responses to climate change.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The noun "response" collocates with the preposition "to". We give a "response to" something. So "responses to climate change" is correct, not "responses of".

◦ Correct: Effective responses to climate change are imperative to protect the world's children and fulfil their rights.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• "responses from", "responses at" and "responses with" are all wrong collocations with "response".

NOTE

• Fixed collocation: response to (a response to a question/crisis/situation), respond to, react to, reply to. The preposition "to" signals what the response is directed at.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

When we _____________ ourselves, we activate a variety of psychological processes that help us achieve our objectives and improve our overall well-being.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. believe in.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Believe in ourselves" means to have confidence in our own abilities. This positively "activates psychological processes that help us achieve our objectives", fitting the sense of the sentence. (स्वयं पर विश्वास करना)

◦ Correct: When we believe in ourselves, we activate a variety of psychological processes ...

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "doubt" ourselves would harm, not help, well-being.

• Option 2 "demolish" (to destroy) and Option 4 "linger" (to stay on) do not fit "ourselves" in this positive context.

NOTE

• "Believe in" = to have faith/confidence in (believe in yourself, believe in God). "Believe" (without "in") = to accept as true (I believe you).

question:
Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word from the given sentence.

The kitten's playful behaivor brought joy to the entire family.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Behaivor.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Behaivor" is misspelt. The correct spelling is "behaviour" (British) or "behavior" (American), meaning the way one acts or conducts oneself. (व्यवहार)

◦ Correct: The kitten's playful behaviour brought joy to the entire family.

• Spelling key (British): BE + HAV + IOUR.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• "Kitten's", "Joy" and "Playful" are all correctly spelt.

NOTE

• Note the "-iour"/"-ior" ending: behaviour (British) / behavior (American). Related: behave (verb), behavioural (adjective). A common error is writing "behaivor" (misplacing the "i").

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word.

Brave
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Cowardly.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Brave" means showing courage and not afraid of danger. Its antonym is "cowardly", meaning lacking courage and easily frightened. (बहादुर का विलोम — कायर)

◦ Example: A brave soldier vs a cowardly deserter.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Boundless" (limitless), Option 2 "Dim" (not bright) and Option 4 "Earthly" (worldly) are unrelated.

NOTE

• Synonyms of brave: courageous, valiant, fearless, bold, gallant. Antonyms: cowardly, timid, fearful, faint-hearted.

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

In the contemporary times, sports and games are emerging as one of the brightest careers. It expects to ___1___ at a very high moral plane. It demands honesty and transparency. Sports further demand continuous practice, hard work and ___2___ training. One must understand that sport not only has physical benefits but also ___3___ concentration and inner strength. Not only this, one who plays feels that ____4___ overall personality has undergone a change for better. Besides, social connectivity or networking, games develop ___5___ spirit in players.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. operate.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Operate" means to function or work in a particular way. Sport is expected to "operate at a very high moral plane", i.e., to function on a high moral level. (कार्य करना / संचालित होना)

◦ Correct: It expects to operate at a very high moral plane.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "dwell" (to live/reside) does not collocate with "at a moral plane" in this sense.

• Option 3 "desynchronise" (to put out of sync) and Option 4 "decide" (to make a choice) do not fit.

NOTE

• "Operate at/on a level/plane" means to function at that standard. Synonyms of operate: function, work, run, perform.

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

In the contemporary times, sports and games are emerging as one of the brightest careers. It expects to ___1___ at a very high moral plane. It demands honesty and transparency. Sports further demand continuous practice, hard work and ___2___ training. One must understand that sport not only has physical benefits but also ___3___ concentration and inner strength. Not only this, one who plays feels that ____4___ overall personality has undergone a change for better. Besides, social connectivity or networking, games develop ___5___ spirit in players.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. relentless.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Relentless" means continuous, persistent and never-stopping. Sport demands "continuous practice, hard work and relentless training", i.e., unrelenting, tireless training. (निरंतर / अथक)

◦ Correct: Sports further demand continuous practice, hard work and relentless training.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "paltry" (very small/trivial), Option 3 "abated" (reduced/lessened) and Option 4 "faltering" (weakening/hesitant) all suggest less effort, which contradicts "continuous practice, hard work".

NOTE

• Synonyms of relentless: unrelenting, persistent, unremitting, incessant, tireless. It matches the idea of "continuous" already in the sentence.

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

In the contemporary times, sports and games are emerging as one of the brightest careers. It expects to ___1___ at a very high moral plane. It demands honesty and transparency. Sports further demand continuous practice, hard work and ___2___ training. One must understand that sport not only has physical benefits but also ___3___ concentration and inner strength. Not only this, one who plays feels that ____4___ overall personality has undergone a change for better. Besides, social connectivity or networking, games develop ___5___ spirit in players.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. boosts.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Boosts" means increases or improves. Sport "not only has physical benefits but also boosts concentration and inner strength", i.e., it enhances them. (बढ़ाता है)

◦ Correct: ... sport not only has physical benefits but also boosts concentration and inner strength.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "deteriorates" (worsens) is the opposite of the positive benefit intended.

• Option 2 "controls" and Option 4 "underlines" (emphasises) do not fit the idea of improving concentration and strength.

NOTE

• Synonyms of boost: increase, improve, enhance, raise, strengthen. The context "physical benefits but also ___ concentration" needs a positive, improving verb.

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

In the contemporary times, sports and games are emerging as one of the brightest careers. It expects to ___1___ at a very high moral plane. It demands honesty and transparency. Sports further demand continuous practice, hard work and ___2___ training. One must understand that sport not only has physical benefits but also ___3___ concentration and inner strength. Not only this, one who plays feels that ____4___ overall personality has undergone a change for better. Besides, social connectivity or networking, games develop ___5___ spirit in players.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. one's.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The passage uses the generic pronoun "one" ("one who plays feels that ..."). The matching possessive is "one's". So "one's overall personality has undergone a change for better". (सामान्य सर्वनाम 'one' का अधिकारवाचक रूप — one's)

◦ Correct: ... one who plays feels that one's overall personality has undergone a change for better.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "their" is plural and does not agree with the singular "one".

• Option 3 "it's" = "it is" (a contraction, not a possessive) — wrong.

• Option 4 "his" excludes other genders and does not match "one".

NOTE

• The pronoun "one" takes the possessive "one's" and the reflexive "oneself". Do not confuse "it's" (it is) with "its" (possessive).

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

In the contemporary times, sports and games are emerging as one of the brightest careers. It expects to ___1___ at a very high moral plane. It demands honesty and transparency. Sports further demand continuous practice, hard work and ___2___ training. One must understand that sport not only has physical benefits but also ___3___ concentration and inner strength. Not only this, one who plays feels that ____4___ overall personality has undergone a change for better. Besides, social connectivity or networking, games develop ___5___ spirit in players.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. sportsmanship.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Sportsmanship" means fair play, respect for opponents and graceful conduct in games. Games "develop sportsmanship spirit in players", which is the most appropriate quality developed through sport. (खेल भावना)

◦ Correct: ... games develop sportsmanship spirit in players.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "captaincy" (the role of a captain), Option 2 "companionship" (friendship) and Option 4 "leadership" (the ability to lead) are narrower and do not capture the "spirit" games are best known for developing.

NOTE

• "Sportsmanship spirit" refers to fairness, team spirit, respect and grace in victory or defeat — a core value promoted through sports.
